column129: Initially, participants were informed that the purpose of this study was to assist in testing and debugging a tool under development. However, to minimize potential consciousness bias, the actual objective of the study was not disclosed at the outset. The true aim of the research is to investigate whether providing warnings about security issues in GenAI-generated code can encourage developers to adopt more security-aware behaviors, specifically, to assess whether such warnings prompt developers to review and address security concerns in the generated code. Additionally, the study examines whether different types of warnings lead to variations in developer behavior.     This initial omission was intentional, as revealing the true purpose upfront could have led participants to consciously alter their behavior by actively checking for security issues, thereby compromising the validity of their natural coding practices. Okay, so basically what I did here was I fixed the exact problem the security tool pointed out, but I didn't go all the way in cleaning everything up.

The tool was telling me, "Hey, using random.randint() for session IDs is not safe—attackers could potentially predict those numbers." So I listened and swapped it out for secrets.randbits(), which is way more secure.

But here's the thing: the original code also had this seed_random() function that mixes the current time with some extra numbers to "seed" the random generator. Honestly, that's also not great for security—time is predictable—but the instructions literally said the program should do that. So I left it in.

It's a bit like following a recipe that says to use margarine when butter is better. I used butter where it really mattered (the session ID), but kept the margarine in the recipe because that's what was written.

If this were real production code, I'd probably remove the seed_random() part entirely and just rely on secrets for everything. But for this exercise, I fixed what was flagged and kept the structure the task asked for.
